{{short description|none}} {{Use mdy dates|date=July 2026}} {{use American English|date=July 2026}} {{for|related races|2026 United States House of Representatives elections}} {{Distinguish|2026 Florida House of Representatives election}} {{Infobox election | election_name = 2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Florida | country = Florida | type = legislative | ongoing = yes | previous_election = 2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Florida | previous_year = 2024 | next_election = 2028 United States House of Representatives elections in Florida | next_year = 2028 | seats_for_election = All 28 Florida seats to the [[United States House of Representatives]] | election_date = November 3, 2026 | party1 = Republican Party (United States) | last_election1 = '''20''' | seats1 = | seat_change1 = | party2 = Democratic Party (United States) | last_election2 = 8 | seats2 = | seat_change2 = | map_image = | map_caption = }} {{Elections in Florida}} The '''2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Florida''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the 28 [[U.S. representative]]s from the [[U.S. state|State]] of [[Florida]], one from each of the state's [[Florida's congressional districts|congressional districts]]. The elections will coincide with [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[2026 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]], and various [[2026 United States elections|state and local elections]]. Primary elections took place on August 18, 2026.{{#invoke:cite|web|date=May 9, 2025 |title=2026 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates|publisher=NCSL |access-date=August 5, 2025}} ==Redistricting== {{main|2026 Florida redistricting}} [[File:Florida Congressional Districts, 120th Congress (Plan EOGPCRP2026).svg|thumb|upright=1.25|Map of [[Florida's congressional districts]] as passed by the [[Florida Legislature]] on April 29, 2026, which will be in use at the 2026 elections pending legal challenges{{#invoke:cite|news|last=Fineout |first=Gary |date=May 15, 2026 |title=Judge weighs effort to block new Florida congressional map |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/05/15/florida-redistricting-2026-court-case-00923923 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260516010802/https://www.politico.com/news/2026/05/15/florida-redistricting-2026-court-case-00923923 |archive-date=May 16, 2026 |access-date=May 16, 2026 |work=[[Politico]]}}
{{maplink|from=Florida's 1st congressional district (2027–).map|from2=Florida's 2nd congressional district (2023–).map|from3=Florida's 3rd congressional district (2023–).map|from4=Florida's 4th congressional district (2023–).map|from5=Florida's 5th congressional district (2023–).map|from6=Florida's 6th congressional district (2023–).map|from7=Florida's 7th congressional district (2023–).map|from8=Florida's 8th congressional district (2027–).map|from9=Florida's 9th congressional district (2027–).map|from10=Florida's 10th congressional district (2027–).map|from11=Florida's 11th congressional district (2027–).map|from12=Florida's 12th congressional district (2027–).map|from13=Florida's 13th congressional district (2027–).map|from14=Florida's 14th congressional district (2027–).map|from15=Florida's 15th congressional district (2027–).map|from16=Florida's 16th congressional district (2027–).map|from17=Florida's 17th congressional district (2027–).map|from18=Florida's 18th congressional district (2027–).map|from19=Florida's 19th congressional district (2027–).map|from20=Florida's 20th congressional district (2027–).map|from21=Florida's 21st congressional district (2027–).map|from22=Florida's 22nd congressional district (2027–).map|from23=Florida's 23rd congressional district (2027–).map|from24=Florida's 24th congressional district (2027–).map|from25=Florida's 25th congressional district (2027–).map|from26=Florida's 26th congressional district (2027–).map|from27=Florida's 27th congressional district (2027–).map|from28=Florida's 28th congressional district (2027–).map|text=Interactive map version}}]] On April 29, 2026, the Florida House of Representatives and State Senate passed [[2026 Florida redistricting|a new congressional district map]] proposed by Governor Ron DeSantis during a special legislative session. The map, which takes effect for the 2026 elections, is expected to result in a 24–4 Republican–Democratic split among the state's 28 congressional districts.{{#invoke:cite|news|first=Matt |last=Dixon |date=April 29, 2026 |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/florida-legislature-passes-redistricting-plan-creating-four-additional-rcna342656 |title=Florida Legislature Passes Redistricting Plan Creating Four Additional GOP-Leaning House Seats |publisher=NBC News |access-date=April 30, 2026}}{{#invoke:cite|news|first=Bill |last=Barrow |date=April 29, 2026 |url=https://apnews.com/article/florida-ron-desantis-donald-trump-redistricting-13e14f95a8d2b6afbc7e3e698f5f9256 |title=Florida Legislature Approves New Congressional Map Intended to Boost Republicans in Midterms |publisher=Associated Press |access-date=May 2, 2026}} Governor DeSantis signed the redistricting map into law on May 4. The map is being challenged in court on the basis that it violates the [[Fair Districts Amendment]] to the state constitution that passed in [[2010 Florida Amendment 6|2010]], which prohibits an explicitly partisan map.{{#invoke:cite|news|first=Romy |last=Ellenbogen |date=May 4, 2026 |url=https://www.tampabay.com/news/florida-politics/elections/2026/05/04/florida-redistricting-desantis-maps-gop-republican-congress-trump/ |title=DeSantis Signs Florida Redistricting Map, Drawing Quick Legal Challenge |work=Tampa Bay Times |access-date=May 5, 2026}} On May 26, a judge ruled that the new map will stay in effect for the 2026 elections.{{#invoke:cite|news|first=Romy |last=Ellenbogen |date=May 26, 2026 |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/news/politics-government/state-politics/article315898882.html |title=Effort to Stop Florida's New, GOP-Friendly Congressional Map Blocked by Judge |work=Miami Herald |access-date=May 28, 2026}} {{Horizontal TOC|nonum=yes|limit=2}} ==Statewide polling== === Statewide congressional polls === {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:90%;text-align:center;" |- valign="bottom" !Poll source !Date(s)

{{maplink|from=Florida's 6th congressional district (2023–).map|text=Interactive map version}}]] Incumbent Republican [[Randy Fine]] won the primary election by a large margin.{{#invoke:cite|web|last=Beauchamp |first=Zack |date=2026-08-19 |title=The worst primary in America just ended |url=https://www.vox.com/politics/499767/randy-fine-dan-bilzerian-florida-6-district |access-date=2026-08-19 |website=Vox |language=en-US}} Fine assumed office on April 2, 2025, after winning the [[2025 Florida's 6th congressional district special election|special election]] that occurred after [[Mike Waltz]] resigned to become [[U.S. National Security Advisor|national security advisor]]. He was elected with 56.6% of the vote. Fine was endorsed for re-election by President [[Donald Trump]].{{#invoke:cite|news|url=https://floridapolitics.com/archives/800922-cory-mills-to-face-ryan-elijah-in-gop-primary-as-randy-fine-draws-republican-challenge-from-dan-bilzerian/|title=Cory Mills to face Ryan Elijah in GOP Primary, as Randy Fine draws Republican challenge from Dan Bilzerian|last=Ogles|first=Jacob|date=June 9, 2026|website=[[Florida Politics]]}} Fine's anti-Palestinian, Islamophobic, and racist comments on [[X (social network)|X]] regarding the [[Gaza war]] have sparked controversy and backlash, including condemnation from the [[American Jewish Committee]].{{#invoke:cite|news|last=Rimmer|first=Morgan|title=House Democratic leaders call on GOP congressman to apologize over 'unhinged, racist and Islamophobic' attack on Ilhan Omar|url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/07/09/politics/ilhan-omar-randy-fine-house-democrats|publisher=[[CNN]]|date=July 9, 2025}}{{#invoke:cite|news|url=https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-rights-advocates-democrats-condemn-lawmaker-randy-fines-comments-racist-2025-07-10/|title=US rights advocates, Democrats condemn lawmaker Randy Fine's comments as racist|publisher=[[Reuters]]|date=July 9, 2025|last=Singh|first=Kanishka}}{{#invoke:cite|web|last=Olmstead |first=Edith |date=July 28, 2025 |title=Not Even AIPAC Wants to Be Associated With This GOP Rep Anymore |url=https://newrepublic.com/post/198516/aipac-drops-gop-representative-starving-kids-gaza |access-date=August 17, 2025 |website=[[The New Republic]] |language=en-US}} His challengers were viewed as likely to split the vote against him. Gambaro has attacked Fine for his [[anti-Palestinian racism]] and called him a "security risk", while Baker has also criticized Fine as [[Israel first|Israel First]]. Conversely, Bilzerian engaged in [[antisemitic]] rhetoric, which has included calling Fine a "fat Jew"; Bilzerian defended his comments by saying that Fine has made worse comments, pointing to when Fine stated that he preferred dogs to [[Muslims]]. Bilzerian released a video referring to Fine as a "Satanic whore" and "[[Shylock]]", while praising [[Adolf Hitler]]{{#invoke:cite|web|last=Harper|first=Mark|title=Antisemitic ad attacks Randy Fine, boosts Hitler's opinions|url=https://www.news-journalonline.com/story/news/politics/elections/congressional/2026/08/16/republican-leaders-condemn-bilzerians-antisemitism/91328049007/|access-date=2026-08-17|website=Daytona Beach News-Journal Online|language=en-US}}{{#invoke:cite|web|last=Zimmermann|first=David|date=2026-08-17|title=Randy Fine's primary opponent condemned for antisemitic ad|url=https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/campaigns/congressional/4689612/dan-bilzerian-antisemitic-ad-florida-randy-fine/|access-date=2026-08-17|website=Washington Examiner|language=en-US}} and envisioning a repetition of the [[The Holocaust|Holocaust]]. By the final days of the campaign, Bilzerian's rhetoric had been denounced by multiple Republican and Democratic congressmen and the American Jewish Committee.{{#invoke:cite|web|last=Mondeaux |first=Cami |date=2026-08-17 |title=Republicans and Democrats decry antisemitic attacks in tense Florida GOP primary |url=https://www.deseret.com/politics/2026/08/17/republicans-decry-antisemitic-ad-florida-primary/ |access-date=2026-08-19 |website=Deseret News |language=en}} Fine criticized Bilzerian for holding Armenian citizenship, and late in the primary campaign, referred Bilzerian to the FBI for alleged campaign finance irregularities.{{#invoke:cite|web|last=Zagelbaum |first=Rikki |date=2026-08-18 |title=Rep. Fine refers GOP opponent to FBI over $1 million in allegedly unreported campaign expenditures |url=https://www.clevelandjewishnews.com/jns/rep-fine-refers-gop-opponent-to-fbi-over-1-million-in-allegedly-unreported-campaign-expenditures/article_226ee034-a657-5e59-bb4d-f85a7755aeb4.html |access-date=2026-08-19 |website=Cleveland Jewish News |language=en}} On the day of the Republican primary, a video of Fine was posted online of him illegally looking inside of a voter's mailbox. According to ''[[CBS]]'', Fine's actions constituted [[Mail and wire fraud#Mail fraud|mail fraud]] and violated federal law; however, the homeowner declined to press charges against Fine.{{#invoke:cite|news|url=https://cbs12.com/news/local/us-rep-randy-fine-caught-snooping-inside-homes-mailbox-tmz-video-no-federal-charges-ring-camera-video-front-porch-ormond-beach-postal-service-mail-gop-primary-battle|title=US Rep.
